title: Unit Economics Dashboard (MVP) — Scope + Priorities (Console & Rollouts)
content:
Doc purpose
- Capture what Product considers “MVP” for the internal Unit Economics dashboard (source of truth for blended $/1M output tokens).
- Make explicit what we are shipping first vs. what we will NOT ship in MVP (to avoid scope creep + cardinality/perf issues).
- Provide a checklist for sign-off with Finance + Platform.

Audience / primary users
- Finance (Laura, Rishi): weekly reporting + tie-out confidence
- Product (Console/Rollouts + Hosted API + Optimize): make decisions on routing defaults, packaging, and rollouts guardrails
- Engineering (Telemetry/Analytics, SRE): detect regressions and attribute to drivers

MVP “north star”
- A Finance-aligned metric definition for blended cost as $/1M output tokens, visible as a trend and sliceable by a small set of stable dimensions.
- Enough drilldown to answer: “Why did our blended cost change week-over-week?” without needing ad-hoc SQL.

In-scope for MVP (what ships)

1) Core metric views (must-have)
A. Blended cost trend
- Chart: daily (default) + weekly aggregation toggle
- Metric: blended $/1M output tokens (canonical definition per ADR)
- Comparison: previous period overlay (e.g., last 7 vs prior 7) OR WoW % change callout
- Time range presets: 7d / 30d / 90d (90d enabled once backfill is done)

B. Cost drivers (explain at a high level)
- Simple breakdown table for top drivers, MVP version:
  - Region mix (change in share across regions)
  - Model mix (change in share across models)
  - Cache hit-rate change (impact estimate, if available)
  - “Other / residual” bucket (do not attempt full causal modeling in MVP)
- Important: The “Explain” panel can be coarse in MVP, but must avoid misleading certainty. Present as attribution estimate + show underlying mix deltas.

C. Slice table (the workhorse)
- Table: blended $/1M output tokens by [dimension], sorted desc by spend proxy (see note) and/or highest cost
- Dimensions supported in MVP:
  1) Model (model family/variant as used in metering)
  2) Region (cloud region)
  3) Customer tier (self_serve / dedicated / private / enterprise)
- Table columns (minimum):
  - blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens
  - output_tokens
  - requests (optional if low effort; ok to defer)
  - cache_hit_rate (optional; ok to include once ENG-2913 lands)
- “Spend proxy” note: We likely don’t have a perfect per-slice dollar spend in MVP; use output_tokens * blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens for ranking and label it clearly (e.g., “estimated blended cost”). Finance sign-off required on naming.

2) Filter model (guardrailed)
- Global filters (MVP):
  - Date range
  - Model (multi-select)
  - Region (multi-select)
  - Customer tier (multi-select)
- Default state:
  - Date: last 30 days
  - All regions
  - All customer tiers
  - “Top models by output tokens” pre-selected? (open question; default “All models” is simplest, but table can be long)
- Guardrails:
  - If user selects >N models (suggest N=20) show warning and force aggregated view only (no per-model breakdown) OR block selection and suggest using search.

3) Drilldowns (prioritized)
Priority 0 (must-have):
- From trend -> open detail page pre-filtered to the same date range + filters.
- From slice table row (e.g., a region) -> drilldown to next dimension (e.g., region -> models within region).

Priority 1 (strongly preferred):
- Pivot path support for “one click” drilldown:
  - Region -> Model
  - Model -> Region
  - Tier -> Region
  - Tier -> Model
- Keep it constrained: max depth 2 in MVP. Avoid arbitrary “add any dimension” pivot builder.

Priority 2 (nice-to-have, only if cheap):
- Link-outs to:
  - relevant rollouts (if a rollout tag exists and is low-cardinality)
  - incidents (manual link or just a free-text “notes” area for now)

4) Exports + sharing (must-have formats)
- CSV export
  - For any table view (slice table + drilldown tables)
  - Must include applied filters in header (or as first rows) to avoid “what am I looking at?” issues.
- PNG export (optional)
  - Prefer deferring unless already supported by Console chart components.
- Shareable link
  - URL encodes filters (date range, model, region, tier) so Finance can link slices in weekly review.
- API export (explicitly not in MVP)
  - We will have backend query endpoints for the UI, but we are not committing to an “official” programmatic export contract in MVP.

5) Access control (MVP expectations)
- Dashboard is internal-only and behind feature flag.
- Tier-level slicing is allowed for broad roles, but any view that reveals discount/credit impacts is NOT included in MVP (see deferrals).
- Basic auditability: log dashboard access events (who/when) if already in the platform patterns; otherwise capture as follow-up.

6) Data confidence UX (minimum)
- Show dataset freshness timestamp (“data as of …”) at top.
- If reconciliation variance is above threshold OR data is incomplete:
  - show a warning banner
  - allow viewing last known good date range
  - avoid mixing partial day data into trend by default (e.g., hide “today” until complete)

Out of scope / explicitly deferred (V2+)

A) High-cardinality / sensitive drilldowns
- Per-customer / account-level slicing (explicitly deferred)
- Per-route, per-runtime_config slicing beyond a small allowlist (deferred; cardinality + perf)
- Per-prompt / per-endpoint path (deferred)
- Any UI that directly surfaces discounts/credits at slice level (restricted and sensitive; defer until RBAC + Finance policy are fully implemented)

B) Full driver attribution / causal modeling
- No promise of “this exact routing change caused +$X” in MVP.
- No Shapley-style decomposition, no automatic root cause. MVP explanation is mix-shift + cache hit change + residual.

C) Real-time / intra-day correctness
- No near-real-time updates; daily partitions are acceptable for MVP.
- No “last hour” view.

D) Multi-metric surface area explosion
- No separate tabs for gross margin %, revenue per token, etc. MVP focuses on cost per 1M output tokens.
- No embedded forecasting.

E) Custom cohorts and saved reports
- No saved filter presets per user/team (beyond shareable links).
- No scheduled email reports from within Console (Finance can export manually for weekly review).

F) Customer-facing version
- Not part of this MVP. Any externalization requires legal/comms review and likely different definitions.

MVP acceptance criteria (Product sign-off checklist)
- Metric shown in dashboard matches canonical definition (ADR) and can be reconciled to billing/metering within agreed tolerance (Finance must sign off on tolerance).
- A Finance user can answer, without SQL:
  1) “What is blended $/1M output tokens last week vs prior week?”
  2) “Which region and model contributed most to the change?”
  3) “Did cache hit-rate meaningfully move, and in which direction?” (if cache metrics included)
- Exports:
  - CSV works and includes filter context.
  - Shareable links reproduce the same view.
- Usability/perf:
  - Default view loads in <5s on corp network.
  - Drilldown table loads in <8s for typical slices.
- Data health UX:
  - Freshness timestamp visible.
  - Warning state triggers when data is stale/incomplete.

Open questions (need decisions)
1) Naming
- “Blended cost” vs “Blended COGS” vs “All-in cost” — propose “Blended cost ($/1M output tokens)” in UI.
- “Estimated blended cost” column in tables — confirm wording with Finance.

2) Default aggregation
- Daily vs weekly default: propose daily with weekly toggle (Finance weekly review uses weekly, Eng prefers daily for regression detection).

3) Model dimension normalization
- Do we show raw model IDs (e.g., vendor/model@version) or product-friendly names? MVP: raw but stable; add alias mapping in V2.

4) Tier mapping correctness
- How do we handle customers migrating tiers mid-period? MVP: use historical correctness per day (Engineering to implement), but UI should not imply “static tier.”

5) Cache metrics readiness
- If cache hit-rate attribution isn’t reliable by launch, MVP should still ship without it rather than block. Put behind a sub-feature flag.

Proposed MVP timeline checkpoints (for internal planning)
- Week 1–2: scope locked + metric definition sign-off with Finance
- Week 3–5: data pipeline + semantic layer stable enough for UI integration
- Week 6–7: Console UI + exports + share links + data freshness banners
- Week 8: internal rollout to Finance/Product + start weekly review cadence

Notes / references
- Canonical metric definition: Confluence ADR-0142 (blended $/1M output tokens)
- Key engineering epic: Linear PM-482
- Data contracts + SLO: Platform/SRE docs (links in tickets)

Changelog
- 2025-02-03 (Marissa): added explicit export requirements + clarified drilldown depth limit (max depth 2)
- 2025-02-06 (Marissa/Alicia): added data confidence UX requirements + tightened deferrals around discounts/credits views
